title: Live Viewer Count
seoTitle: Design "X People Are Viewing This Page" Live Counts
description: Design a live viewer counter — tracking active viewers per page with heartbeats, expiring presence, approximate counting at scale, and pushing updates.
author: Editorial Team

blocks.title: What is a Live Viewer Count?
blocks.text: Travel and shopping sites show messages like "23 people are looking at this hotel right now". The system tracks how many users currently have a page open and keeps the number roughly up to date.

items: While a user has a page open, they should be counted as viewing it.
Users should see the current viewer count for the page they're on.
When users leave (or close the tab), they should stop being counted within about a minute.

blocks.question: What are the non-functional requirements for this system?

items: Counts can be approximate and up to ~30-60 seconds stale.
Must not slow down page loads; failures should just hide the badge.
Scale to millions of concurrent viewers across millions of pages, with hot pages having 100k+ viewers.
**Page**: a hotel, product or listing ID.
**Viewer presence**: (pageId, viewerId) with a last-seen timestamp.
**Viewer count**: the number of active viewers for a page.

blocks.code:
POST /pages/:pageId/heartbeat { viewerId }   (every 20-30s while visible)
GET  /pages/:pageId/viewers -> { count }

blocks.text: 1) Count users while the page is open
The browser sends a **heartbeat** every ~20 seconds while the tab is visible (using the Page Visibility API). Each heartbeat refreshes the viewer's presence for that page with a TTL of ~60 seconds.

Presence is stored per page in a Redis sorted set (`member = viewerId`, `score = lastSeen`). The count is the number of members seen within the last 60 seconds: remove older members (`ZREMRANGEBYSCORE`) and read `ZCARD`. The response is cached for a few seconds per page since everyone viewing it gets the same number.
Viewers who close the tab simply stop heartbeating; their entries age out of the window. A `navigator.sendBeacon` on page hide can remove them immediately as a best effort.
1) How do we count at millions of concurrent viewers?

blocks.title: Store each heartbeat in a database

approach.text: Insert a row per heartbeat and `COUNT(DISTINCT viewer)` over the last minute.

challenges.text: Millions of writes per minute and expensive aggregate queries for every page view.

approach.text: As above: one sorted set per page, trimmed by score.

challenges.text: A hot page with 100k viewers means a big set and many writes on one key.

approach.text: Bucket presence by minute: add each heartbeat to a **HyperLogLog** for `(pageId, currentMinute)`, which uses ~12KB regardless of viewers. The live count is the merged HLL of the last two buckets (`PFCOUNT` on both keys), giving ~1% error. Buckets expire after a few minutes. For very hot pages, aggregate heartbeats in each presence server for a second before writing.

challenges.text: Counts are approximate — perfectly fine for "about 23 people".

blocks.text: 2) Should we poll or push the count?

Polling the count every 30 seconds piggybacks on the heartbeat response — the heartbeat endpoint simply returns the latest cached count. That's far cheaper than maintaining push connections for a badge that only needs minute-level freshness. Push (SSE) is worth it only for pages where the number changes the user's behaviour in seconds.
Return the count in the heartbeat response. One request every 20 seconds serves both "I'm here" and "how many are here?".

quiz.question: How does the system know a user left without an explicit signal?
options: Their heartbeats stop and presence expires after the window
quiz.explanation: Time-based expiry handles closed tabs and crashes.

quiz.question: Why use HyperLogLog for hot pages?
options: Constant small memory with ~1% error regardless of viewer count
quiz.explanation: Approximate cardinality is all a viewer badge needs.

quiz.question: What's an efficient way to deliver the count to the page?
options: Return it in the heartbeat response
quiz.explanation: One periodic request serves both purposes.

quiz.question: Why use the Page Visibility API for heartbeats?
options: To avoid counting tabs left open in the background
quiz.explanation: Only actively visible pages should count as viewers.
